rationale: No-spec round (sdlc-light — no story/spec artifact; confidence forced low). Two major patch findings: CR-001 (admin 'has no Previous-page button on the first page' test lacks a pagination-settled anchor, creating a vacuous-pass risk mirroring the exact anti-pattern the analytics tests guard against with an explicit await findByRole anchor) and CR-002 (ActivityEventsPage — the 7th admin table added in the preceding commit EPMCDME-13275 — is absent from TABLE_CONFIGS, leaving its pagination unverified). Deferred 1 (Teams bot pages — out of stated task scope). Dismissed 5 (copy-paste structure, initial-store-injection design choice, makeLastPage field-name confusion resolved on re-read, makeSinglePage page consistency, redundant assertions). Git workflow and security pass.

standards_review.notes: Both commits match 'EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence' format. Branch 'EPMCDME-13482_pagination-tests-admin-analytics' follows the documented naming pattern.

.gitleaks.toml .codegraph/ exclusion is safe (local development index, no source code or secrets). No credentials, API keys, or real PII in test fixtures. Admin user fixture (is_admin: true) is test-only data.

findings.problem: The 'has no Previous-page button on the first page' test in AdminTablesPagination.integration.test.tsx (parametrized across all 6 table configs, lines ~668-672) asserts absence of the Previous button immediately after 'await screen.findByText(page0Text)' with no intermediate anchor confirming pagination has rendered.
findings.impact: If pagination fails to render entirely due to a component regression, the test still passes because no Previous button is trivially absent. The analogous analytics tests (UserEngagement and AssetReusability) explicitly add 'await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Next page" })' before the negative assertion to anchor on settled pagination state; the admin suite is inconsistent and could mask a full pagination outage.
findings.recommendation: Add 'await screen.findByRole("button", { name: "Next page" })' immediately before the 'expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: "Previous page" })).not.toBeInTheDocument()' line in the admin 'has no Previous-page button' test, matching the settled-anchor pattern used in both analytics test files.

findings.problem: ActivityEventsPage (route '/settings/administration/activity-events', API endpoint GET v1/admin/activity-events) is absent from TABLE_CONFIGS in AdminTablesPagination.integration.test.tsx. This page was added in the immediately preceding commit (EPMCDME-13275) and uses the identical nested pagination shape (pagination.page / per_page / total) and the same shared Table+Pagination component as the other entries. The task description targets 7 admin tables; only 6 are covered.
findings.impact: A pagination regression in the Activity Events admin table — the most recently added paginated admin view — would ship undetected despite this test file's stated purpose of covering admin table pagination.
findings.recommendation: Add an ActivityEventsPage entry to TABLE_CONFIGS: { label: 'Activity Events', route: '/settings/administration/activity-events', apiUrl: 'v1/admin/activity-events', page0Response: { data: [...], pagination: { page: 0, per_page: 10, total: 25 } }, page1Response: { data: [...], pagination: { page: 1, per_page: 10, total: 25 } }, page0Text: '<first-row-text>', page1Text: '<second-row-text>' }. No new helpers are required.
